projectDescription: A formal model checker for distributed systems that uses a YAML-based DSL to describe microservice architectures and statically verifies cross-component correctness properties such as ordering, serialization, idempotency, and recoverability.
keyFeatures: YAML-based DSL for modeling microservice architectures (services, schemas, topics, operations, state machines, data models)
Static verification of correctness properties: serialization, ordering, idempotency, recoverability, and result-replay consistency
Epistemic proof verdicts — proven, unknown, or disproven — with detailed evidence and assumptions
Interactive single-file HTML visualization of the architecture graph and obligation results
Coinductive (greatest-fixpoint) analysis for mutually dependent requirements across cascading operations
Formal distinction between unspecified (unknown) and explicitly negative guarantees
CLI-driven workflow: validate a model, run the verifier, and export a JSON prover report
Embeddable Rust library API for programmatic model parsing, validation, and verification
publicApiSurface: DSL top-level keys: revision, services, schemas, data_models, topics, state_machines, operations
Requirement kinds: serialization, ordering, idempotency (with result_replay), recoverability
ProverReport JSON format (format: 2) with obligations array
